dct_description_sm: Cumberland Sound, an inlet on Baffin Island, Nunavut, is undergoing changes in sea ice cover, which is affecting the marine food web. A small population of beluga whales (Delphinapterus leucas) inhabits Cumberland Sound year round and this population is currently listed as threatened. An understanding of their foraging behaviour is vital for determining how best to conserve the population. Currently, relatively little is known about the foraging behaviour of these belugas, but we expected that food web changes, primarily an increased abundance of capelin in the region, would have an impact on their diet. We evaluated fatty acids in blubber samples collected from subsistence hunted belugas in Cumberland Sound from the 1980s to 2010 to gain a better understanding of their foraging behaviour.
dct_title_s: Blubber fatty acid values for Cumberland Sound Belugas
